newsitem.title: USA: POLL-Fed seen holding rates firm at Tuesday's FOMC.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Fed seen holding rates firm at Tuesday's FOMC.

text.p: The Federal Reserve will stand pat on short-term interest rates after its monetary policy-setting arm concludes its meeting on Tuesday, economists surveyed by Reuters agreed unanimously.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled to meet in Washington at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT and will announce its decision at about 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
All 31 economists polled by Reuters said the central bank will hold the key federal funds target rate steady at 5.50 percent.
Citing healthy economic growth with virtually no concerns about inflation, the experts said they see no need for the Fed to apply the brakes just yet.
"You still have the economy in a sweet spot," said Carey Leahey, chief U.S. economist at High Frequency Economics.
He said the 0.6-percent increase in July retail sales suggested the economy continues to grow at a modest pace amid quiescent inflation numbers.

For example, the 0.1-percent decline in the July Producer Price Index (PPI) was a record seventh consecutive monthly drop. And the 0.2-percent rise in the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) was on target with Wall Street's expectations and viewed as nonthreatening.
Nevertheless, it is widely known that the Fed looks for signs of future price and wage increases rather than focusing on the past.
More than two-thirds of the respondents projected the Fed would rein in credit at least once more this year, but only five forecast a move at the FOMC gathering September 30.

"I think (the Fed) is still going to take out a little insurance in the form of a rate hike ... going forward," said Bank of Boston chief economist Wayne Ayers, who was calling for a 25-basis point rate hike at the September meeting.
For now, however, Ayers said it was difficult for Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan to make a preemptive move when economic growth was unburdened by inflationary pressures.

The FOMC last acted preemptively to stave off inflation on March 25, when it boosted the funds rate by 25 basis points. The Fed Board last moved on the discount rate in January 1996, lowering it by 25 basis points to 5.00 percent.
After Tuesday, the FOMC is scheduled to meet on September 30, November 12, and December 16.
